oracle_provenance: Independent Woodworth (1938) rigid-sphere far-field worked examples, cross-checked at 90 degrees against the commonly cited ~650-660 microsecond human maximum ITD; not copied from any shared Skill fixture.
scope: Bounded spherical-head ITD sanity baseline for a claimed HRTF/rendering ITD at a single azimuth; not individualized HRTF measurement.

cases.question: Does a claimed ITD close to the spherical-head prediction at 45 degrees pass within a tight tolerance?
At exactly 90 degrees (the model's own maximum), does the prediction match the well-known ~656-microsecond human maximum ITD for a typical head radius?
Must a head radius outside the plausible human range be rejected rather than silently used?

By the sphere's own front-back symmetry, must 135 degrees (back hemisphere) predict the identical ITD magnitude as 45 degrees (front), discriminating a genuine model limit from a simple front/back convention mismatch?
When a claimed ITD deviates well beyond tolerance from the spherical-head prediction, is that flagged rather than silently accepted?
